why: The student turned the switch into an else-if chain whose structure is correct: case 1 maps to the first test, the fall-through of case 2 into case 3 becomes value == 2 || value == 3, and default becomes the final else. But 'elif' is Python and not Java (Java needs 'else if'), so this is a relational answer with an error.

concepts.quote: if (value == 1) result = 30; elif (value == 2 || value == 3) result = -10; else result = 5;
concepts.why: The answer relates the switch to an else-if chain whose final else catches the remaining cases, but 'elif' is not Java syntax and should be 'else if'.
Each case label becomes a correct boolean test in parentheses that guards one assignment.
It uses an inclusive || correctly to express the cases that fall through together.
Each branch keeps the switch's assignment unchanged and correct.
The answer makes no claim about short-circuit evaluation.
There are no side-effecting expressions in the code or the answer.
